patch.value: A truncated list-all answer is consumed as if it were complete

Every list-all read in this package takes .items from the pm list-all --json envelope without checking the envelope's completeness receipt. Verified on this host against the 682-item workspace: pm 2026.8.14 returned 10 items with truncated=true, and the exporter happily emitted a 10-item export reporting success (98% of rows missing). 2026.8.15 fixes the default, but truncated can still go true under an output budget and completeness.status can go partial when items are unreadable — each of those must refuse loudly instead of producing a partial result that reports success. Related: the @unbrained/pm-cli dependency resolves through a floating range (>=2026.8.3), which is how the 2026.8.14 regression reached this package with no diff to review.

value.text:
Wired all four refusal signals into the single list-all call site (readPmItems, which feeds buildBeadsFromWorkspace / runExport / readWorkspaceBeadIds fallback): truncated===true, has_more===true, completeness.status!==complete (missing receipt also trips), omission_receipt.has_omissions===true. Each refusal is a CommandError naming the tripped signal and the count-vs-total figures; no partial list, no warning-and-continue. maxBuffer kept (64 MiB, PM_JSON_MAX_BUFFER override) and the ENOBUFS null-status case is classified explicitly. Chose REFUSAL over a paging loop: this package has no legitimate use for a partial page.

Revert-proof (removed only the assertListAllComplete(parsed) call, rebuilt, ran the new tests): all four refusal tests failed with 'AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Missing expected exception' (truncated / has_more / completeness.status / omission_receipt at test/smoke.test.ts:1610 et al.); happy-path test still passed as expected. Review round 2 (CodeRabbit + Greptile on PR #69) — three findings adopted, one declined.

ADOPTED — `omission_receipt` mutation assumed the receipt exists (test/smoke.test.ts). The baseline test accepts `omission === undefined`, so on a CLI that omits the receipt the mutation assigned through `undefined` and threw a TypeError *outside* `assert.throws`: the test would have failed with the wrong error instead of proving the refusal. The mutation now creates the receipt when absent.

ADOPTED — `readPmItems surfaces child failures through the seam` had no `{ skip: !hasPmCli() }` guard while calling `realEnvelope()`. On a host without the pm CLI it failed its `init.status === 0` assertion rather than skipping. All four cases inject a seam and never reach a real child process, so the test now uses a temp directory and needs no CLI at all — strictly more coverage than adding a skip.

ADOPTED (Greptile P1, root cause was larger than reported) — the lockfile still carried the pre-floor exact peer `2026.8.15` while package.json declares `>=2026.8.15`, which would fail the release workflow's `npm ci` synchronization check. Regenerating the lockfile fixed that, but the audit also found `manifest.json` still advertising `pm_min_version: 2026.7.28` — the pm host's own load-time floor — while the code refuses on a completeness receipt that only exists from 2026.8.15. A 2026.7.28 host would have loaded an extension that cannot work against it. Floor corrected to 2026.8.15.

DECLINED — CodeRabbit asked the packaging test to assert `declared === peer` exact equality. That was written against the earlier exact-peer revision; commit 1852bf1 deliberately moved the peer to a `>=` floor because an exact peer pin makes every later CLI patch a peer conflict for consumers under strict peer resolution, turning a compatibility statement into a lockstep release dependency. The test correctly asserts floor *shape* plus a `>= 2026.8.15` bound.

DURABLE FIX — nothing bound package.json's peer floor to manifest.json's `pm_min_version`, which is why the manifest could sit three releases stale while every file stayed internally consistent. A regression test now binds them; reverting the floor to 2026.7.28 makes it fail (verified).

value.text:
Review round 3 (Greptile + CodeRabbit on PR #69) — three findings adopted, one declined.

ADOPTED (Greptile P1, and it was right about a real hole) — `readPmItems` refuses an incomplete or unusable `list-all` envelope, but `readWorkspaceBeadIds` caught that refusal and returned `undefined`, and `readAndValidateBeads` had a second `catch` doing the same. The refusal was therefore defeated one level up.

The consequence is a MISDIAGNOSIS, which is worse than a missing check: with `workspaceBeadIds === undefined`, `validateBeadsText` reports a dependency that exists in the workspace as a hard `dangling_dependency` error. The import gate then rejects a valid file and blames the operator's input for a workspace read that failed silently. Reproduced by reverting the fix, which yields exactly:

```
line 1 [dangling_dependency]: dependency references unknown bead id "bd-missing"
```

Fixed by distinguishing the two cases rather than by removing the catch. "No workspace here" is legitimate and the cross-check is optional, so an ordinary read failure still degrades to "no workspace data". A completeness refusal is not that — the workspace answered and the answer is provably partial — so those now throw `IncompleteWorkspaceReadError` (a `CommandError` subclass) and both catch sites re-throw it. Regression test drives a fake `pm` emitting a truncated envelope through the real import gate and asserts the refusal arrives with `truncated=true` and WITHOUT the false `dangling_dependency` text.

ADOPTED (CodeRabbit) — the list-all seam discarded its argv, so nothing asserted what the production read actually sends. `--full --include-body` is what keeps descriptions, tags and dependency edges out of the brief projection, and the ABSENCE of `--limit` is what makes the read the whole workspace. Both were invisible to every existing test, because the receipt-based refusals all inject their own envelope and never exercise the argv. The seam now captures it and the test asserts the complete argv plus the explicit no-`--limit` requirement. Verified non-vacuous: adding `--limit 1000` to the production call fails it.

ADOPTED (CodeRabbit, trivial) — the new floor test repeated the `/^>=\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/` literal that `MINIMUM_VERSION_RANGE` already defines with its rationale. Now reuses the constant.

DECLINED (CodeRabbit) — reword the CHANGELOG entry to state the fix rather than the defect. The entry is not hand-written: `pm-changelog` generates it from this item's title, and the line sits under `### Fixed`, where naming the bug is the Keep a Changelog convention and what all 20 sibling packages do. Rewording here would require retitling this Issue to describe a fix rather than the defect it was filed for — degrading the tracker to improve the changelog. The same finding was raised on pm-starter #58 and declined for the same reason. The constructive fix is a dedicated release-note field in pm-changelog, tracked separately.

112 tests + the new cases pass, release:check green.
